page: Microsoft Azure F4as_v6 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Fasv6 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 vCPUs with 4 physical cores and a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% at 3080.78 and Geekbench single-core scoring in the top 25% at 2106.0. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12286.75 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6784.0. Memory performance shows a distinct tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 590.47 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 37.88 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains average at 28.0 GB/sec.

The server is suitable for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance, such as text processing, which scored in the top 25% on Geekbench. It is also capable of handling general-purpose tasks like static web serving with 8.39 GB/sec throughput, Redis SET operations at 10.43 million operations per second, and software compilation. However, it exhibits performance limitations for larger models, with prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model falling into the bottom 25% at 23.37 tokens per second. Qualitatively, the dedicated core allocation and high single-core performance provide solid resource density for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage.
